S65.01.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app (Electron host); no guided wizard found
S65.01.note: Code shows a toggle plus permission rows, not a guided multi-step setup; the Expected 'guided' part looks different from the code.
steps: Open Settings… from the app menu.
Under Desktop app, click Computer use.
Turn on the switch labelled Any app.

Look for the rows Accessibility and Screen Recording with Open System Settings buttons and compare with Expected: the permissions are shown and linked, but no step-by-step wizard was found in the code.
S65.01.where: Settings… (app menu) > Desktop app > Computer use > Any app

labels.text: Computer use: moving the pointer, clicking and typing

S65.02.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app
S65.02.note: The same rows also appear under Desktop app > Permissions (SYSTEM_HINT text in DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx).
steps: Open Settings… and go to Desktop app > Computer use.
Turn on Any app.
Read the Accessibility and Screen Recording rows: each shows what it is for and a status such as Not asked yet or Allowed.
Where the status needs action, click Open System Settings for that row and compare with Expected: each permission has a purpose line.
S65.02.where: Settings… (app menu) > Desktop app > Computer use (with Any app on) > Accessibility and Screen Recording rows

S65.03.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app and one installed app to test with
S65.03.note: The list cannot add an app directly; an app is added only through the permission dialog during a task. The session-allow button label was not confirmed.
steps: Open Settings… and go to Desktop app > Computer use, with Any app on.
Ask AGI in chat to work in an app, for example TextEdit, while Computer use is on.
When the permission dialog appears, choose the allow option it offers (Deny is the refuse button).
Go back to Computer use and look under Allowed apps for that app; each row offers Remove, and an empty list reads None yet.
S65.03.where: Settings… (app menu) > Desktop app > Computer use > Allowed apps

S65.04.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app and an installed app to refuse
S65.04.note: Refused rows show Always refused or Refused until you quit Desktop; Ask again restores them.
steps: Open Settings… and go to Desktop app > Computer use.
Under Refused apps, click Add app (only shown when the Desktop can refuse apps).
Type in Search apps and pick an app in Installed apps.
Check that the app now appears under Refused apps, then ask AGI in chat to control it and compare with Expected: it should not run.
S65.04.where: Settings… (app menu) > Desktop app > Computer use > Refused apps > Add app

S65.06.needs: a Mac with two displays and a computer-use task
S65.06.note: The display choice is a tool parameter the agent sends, not a control in the UI; the id must come from a previous screenshot listing.
steps: On a Mac with two displays, with Computer use on, ask AGI in chat to take a screenshot, then ask it to look at the second display.
Open the activity under the reply and check the step reads Looked at display 2 (the number is passed by the agent).
Compare with Expected: the screenshot should come from the chosen display.
S65.06.where: Effect seen in the chat activity: Looked at display N

S65.07.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on and an app to act in
S65.07.note: A picture appears only when the step returns one; I did not confirm the exact live timing.
steps: With Computer use on (Settings… > Desktop app > Computer use > Any app), send a chat request that makes AGI click or look at the screen.
While it runs, open the activity shown under the reply.
Look for each screen step card with a picture of the screen and the caption Screen after: followed by the action.
Compare with Expected: the picture should match what the agent saw.
S65.07.where: Chat, under the reply: activity step cards with a screenshot

S65.09.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app
S65.09.note: Searched ComputerUseSettings.tsx and ComputerUseControlBar.tsx: they show the phase text but no app name. The app name is only in step text (In front: <app>) in apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/device-steps.ts, which the model reads. No on-screen app label found.

S65.10.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app
S65.10.note: Searched ComputerUseSettings.tsx, ComputerUseControlBar.tsx and the step text in device-steps.ts: no window label is shown to the user. The window is read natively in apps/desktop/electron/native/macos/agi-input.swift, but no UI text using it was found.

S65.11.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on
S65.11.note: The prompt text is set in apps/desktop/electron/runtime/computerUseSteps.ts; the dialog button labels were not confirmed.
steps: Turn on Computer use (Settings… > Desktop app > Computer use > Any app).
In chat, ask AGI to paste text into an app with Command+V.
When the dialog appears, read its reason about the clipboard and choose Deny or allow.
Open Settings… > Capabilities > Local access > Permissions and look for Read the clipboard; compare with Expected: it needs its own answer.
S65.11.where: Chat (computer use on): ask AGI to copy or paste with the keyboard; then Settings… > Capabilities > Local access > Permissions

S65.12.needs: a Mac with the Desktop app and a test folder
S65.12.note: Local access is a Desktop-only section shown under Capabilities.
steps: Open Settings… and click Capabilities, then find Local access.
Under Folders, click Add a folder and choose a folder in the picker.
Check the folder is listed under Folders.
Click Remove on that folder, confirm Remove access in the dialog, and compare with Expected: the folder is no longer listed.
S65.12.where: Settings… (app menu) > Capabilities > Local access > Folders > Add a folder

S65.13.needs: a Desktop app and an installed app to open
S65.13.note: A missing app gives an error that names it; the exact wording was not captured here.
steps: Turn on Settings… > Desktop app > Computer use > Any app.
In chat, ask AGI to open TextEdit.
Allow the permission prompt if one appears.
Look for the TextEdit window opening on the Mac and compare with Expected.
S65.13.where: Chat (computer use on): ask AGI to open an app, for example TextEdit

S65.14.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on and TextEdit
steps: Turn on Settings… > Desktop app > Computer use > Any app, and open TextEdit.
In chat, ask AGI to click the New Document button and type a short word.
Open the activity under the reply and look for the step lines Clicked at ... and Typed.
Compare with Expected: the text should appear in the app.
S65.14.where: Chat (computer use on): send a request to click and type in an app, then the activity under the reply

S65.15.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on and a scrollable window
steps: Turn on Computer use and open a long page or document in an app.
In chat, ask AGI to scroll down in that window.
Open the activity under the reply and look for the step line Scrolled at ...
Compare with Expected: the window should scroll.
S65.15.where: Chat (computer use on): ask AGI to scroll in an app, then the activity under the reply

S65.16.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on and a draggable item
steps: Turn on Computer use and open an app with a draggable item.
In chat, ask AGI to drag the item to another place.
Open the activity under the reply and look for the step line Dragged from ... to ...
Compare with Expected: the item should move.
S65.16.where: Chat (computer use on): ask AGI to drag an item, then the activity under the reply

S65.19.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on
S65.19.note: The bar's placement on screen was not verified in the code read.
steps: Start a computer-use task in chat with Computer use on.
While AGI is working, move the mouse or type.
Look for the bar text Paused. You have the screen. with the hint It paused when you moved the pointer or typed.
Compare with Expected: AGI should stop instead of fighting for the mouse. Then click Hand back to continue.
S65.19.where: The Computer use bar: Paused. You have the screen.

S65.20.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on
S65.20.note: Escape is the stop key (COMPUTER_USE_STOP_SHORTCUT); the Stop button also appears in Settings > Desktop app > Computer use.
steps: Start a computer-use task in chat with Computer use on.
While AGI is working, press Escape, or open the File menu and click Stop Computer Use.
Look for the Computer use bar to disappear, or the Stop button to turn off, and check the chat stops.
Compare with Expected: all computer control should end at once.
S65.20.where: Press Escape while AGI is active, or File > Stop Computer Use

S65.21.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on
S65.21.note: The same Take over button is in Settings > Desktop app > Computer use.
steps: Start a computer-use task while AGI is active.
Click Take over on the Computer use bar (or File > Take Over Screen Control).
Look for the text Paused. You have the screen. and the button now reading Hand back.
Compare with Expected: AGI should hold still while you use the mouse.
S65.21.where: Computer use bar > Take over, or File > Take Over Screen Control

S65.22.needs: a Desktop app with a paused computer-use task
S65.22.note: The Hand the screen back? dialog is in apps/desktop/electron/runtime/computerUseSteps.ts; I did not confirm which click opens it.
steps: While AGI is paused, click Hand back on the Computer use bar (or File > Hand Back Screen Control).
If a dialog titled Hand the screen back? appears, click Hand back in it.
Look for the bar to return to AGI is using your computer.
Compare with Expected: AGI should continue the task.
S65.22.where: Computer use bar > Hand back, or File > Hand Back Screen Control

S65.23.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on and a test app
S65.23.note: The review text comes from the agent or a password-field check (computerUseSteps.ts).
steps: Turn on Computer use and open a test app with a password field or a message box.
In chat, ask AGI to type a password or send a short message.
When the dialog titled Check this step appears, read the message that starts Desktop wants to.
Click Deny and check the step does not run, then repeat and choose Allow once and compare with Expected.
S65.23.where: Chat (computer use on): ask AGI to type into a password field or send a message

S65.25.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on
S65.25.note: There is no separate receipt screen; success or failure display in the activity was not fully confirmed.
steps: Run a computer-use task in chat with Computer use on.
Open the activity under the reply.
Look for one line per action, such as Clicked, Scrolled at or Looked at the screen, and any error line.
Compare with Expected: each action should be recorded and show whether it worked.
S65.25.where: Chat, activity under the reply: the step lines

labels.text: Finder can open, move and delete any file you can, so controlling it reaches every file on this computer.
System Settings changes how this computer is set up, including its privacy and security settings.

S65.26.needs: a Desktop app with computer use on
S65.26.note: Missing apps give No app called ... is installed. The refusal for a blocked app is written for the model, so the chat wording may vary.
steps: Turn on Computer use with Any app.
In chat, ask AGI to control Finder or System Settings.
When the permission dialog appears, read the reason text about what the app can reach.
Compare with Expected: the product should say why it cannot or should not control that app.
S65.26.where: Chat (computer use on): ask AGI to control Finder or System Settings

S65.27.needs: a cloud task with a linked computer that is offline
S65.27.note: Found the wait notice Waiting for <computer> to come online in apps/web/lib/device-steps/device-clearance-step.ts and the wait limit in apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow.ts, but did not find the screen that shows it. Searched those files only.

S65.28.needs: a Desktop app with an app already allowed
S65.28.note: The wording AGI uses after a revoke comes from the model; the code text asks the user to allow the app.
steps: Open Settings… and go to Desktop app > Computer use.
Under Allowed apps, click Remove on an app.
Ask AGI in chat to control that app again.
Compare with Expected: AGI should stop and say how to allow it again, with Ask again or the permission prompt.
S65.28.where: Settings… (app menu) > Desktop app > Computer use > Allowed apps > Remove

S65.29.needs: a paid plan, a second device, and the Desktop app
S65.29.note: Code says Remote Control comes with paid plans. The owner's notes say it is hidden in v1 (2026-11-14), so check the build before testing.
steps: In the Desktop app, open Settings… > Capabilities > Remote Control and click Pair a phone.
Click Copy link for a browser.
On another device, open that link, paste it in the box on the page, and send a task.
Compare with Expected: the task should run on your own Mac.
S65.29.where: Settings… (app menu) > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone, then Copy link for a browser
